words.gloss: basti (enema); mishap, complication; siddhi: success, accomplishment, i.e. the successful treatment of the mishaps of basti

hindi: अब इसके बाद हम बस्ति की व्यापत्तियों यानी गड़बड़ियों की सिद्धि का व्याख्यान करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall explain the siddhi (success, accomplishment) of the mishaps of basti (enema): the Bastivyāpattisiddhi.
notes: Chapter-opening formula. Title read as basti-vyāpatti-siddhi, "the accomplishment (successful treatment) of the mishaps of basti". The word siddhi is kept; "successful treatment" is an interpretive gloss.

words.gloss: vibandha: obstruction, retention (binding up); gaurava: heaviness; ādhmāna: distension, bloating; śiraḥ-ruj: head-pain (headache); vāhana: carrying, conveying (sense obscure here); ūrdhva-ga: going upward

kukṣi: belly; śūla: pain; aṅga: limb, body; ruci: liking, taste (sense of aṅga-ruci obscure); dhmā: blowing, puffing (a bare stem; doubtful here); hṛd: heart (print 'hat', see text_flags); pīḍā: pain, pressure; kartana: cutting (cutting pain); srava: flow, discharge

hindi: विबन्ध यानी रुकावट, भारीपन, आध्मान यानी पेट का फूलना, सिर की पीड़ा, वाहन, जिसका अर्थ यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, और ऊपर की ओर जाने वाले। पेट का शूल, अंग-रुचि, ध्मा, हृदय की पीड़ा, कर्तन और स्राव।
english: Vibandha (obstruction, retention), heaviness, ādhmāna (distension), head-pain, vāhana, and (ones) going upward. Belly-pain (kukṣiśūla), aṅga-ruci, dhmā, heart-pain, cutting pain (kartana) and flow (srava).

text_flags.why: possible: 'hat' for 'hṛt' (lost ṛ-sign; the words give hṛd, heart); heart-pain fits the list (compare hṛcchūla in 18)

notes:
line 05.06.2: GROUPING: lines 05.06.2, 05.06.3 and 05.06.4 read as one statement: 2 and 3 are lists, and 4 gives the cause (non-application and over-application of basti); no verb in 2 or 3. The list in 2 has six members as read here. "vāhana" (lit. "carrying, conveying") is obscure as a complication name; it may be a shortened form (for example pravāhaṇa, "straining"), but this is only a guess and is not applied; the printed word is kept. "ūrdhvaga" is taken as a list member, "(one) going upward" (compare line 05.06.37, where the wind goes upward). Modern equivalents: vibandha = constipation or retention of stool/wind (probable); ādhmāna = abdominal distension, bloating (standard); śiroruj = headache (standard).
line 05.06.3: GROUPING: continues the list of 2; the statement is completed in 4. Members as read: kukṣiśūla, aṅgaruci, dhmā, hṛtpīḍā, kartana, srava (six). The printed "aṅgaruci" and "dhmā" are obscure: aṅga-ruci literally "liking of the body/limbs", possibly a mis-print of a pain-word or of aruci (distaste for food), and "dhmā" is a bare stem (√dhmā "blow") that may be a truncated form of ādhmāna or dhmāna; none of these readings is applied, the printed forms are kept and translated literally. The words are not corrected in the text_flags because no single correction is sure. Modern equivalents: kukṣiśūla = colicky belly pain (standard); kartana = cutting pain (standard).

words.gloss: not (a-); oiled; sweated; body: of one whose body is neither oiled nor sweated (a- governs both, see notes)
heavy; koṣṭha (storehouse, belly); of one whose koṣṭha is heavy

hindi: बस्ति के अयोग यानी प्रयोग न होने से और अतियोग यानी अधिक प्रयोग से छह और छह आपत्तियाँ होती हैं। जिसका शरीर स्निग्ध और स्वेदित नहीं है और जिसका कोष्ठ भारी है, उसमें प्रयुक्त।
english: From non-application (ayoga) and from over-application (atiyoga) of the basti (enema) there are six and six mishaps. Applied to one whose body is not oiled and not sweated, and whose koṣṭha (storehouse, belly) is heavy.

text_flags.why: possible: stray anusvara; "aṃsnigdha" is not a word, "asnigdha" (not oily) fits the sense and metre

notes:
line 05.06.4: Sandhi: ṣaṭṣaḍāpadaḥ = ṣaṭ ṣaṭ āpadaḥ ("six, six"). Read with 2 and 3. Whether the six of 2 are those of non-application and the six of 3 those of over-application is not stated in the text and is not assumed here. "ayoga/atiyoga" are kept literally as non- and over-application.
line 05.06.5: Elliptical: the noun "basti" is supplied only in 7; no noun is added in the translation. The negative a- is taken to govern both snigdha and svinna ("neither oiled nor sweated"), the natural sense; the alternative "not oiled, but sweated" is grammatically possible but less likely. The print has a stray anusvara in "aṃsnigdha". The sentence continues through 6 into 7 (verb in 8: karoti).

english: Cold, or with little oil, salt, drug and quantity, or even thick. The basti, having agitated that doṣa and not expelling it because of weakness,

notes:
line 05.06.6: Continues 5 (the noun basti is supplied only in 7). The print omits the avagraha of śīto 'lpa- (śītaḥ + alpa-); the same omission recurs in 27 ("yuktolpavīryo" for yukto 'lpavīryo"), recorded here once. "śīta" is therefore a separate word ("cold") and alpa begins the bahuvrīhi. Ambiguity: whether alpa ("little") applies to all four of sneha, lavaṇa, dravya, mātrā is not fixed by the compound; the plain reading is taken.
line 05.06.7: The sentence continues in 8 (verb karoti). The subject of the weakness (durbalatva) is not stated; the natural reading is the basti, but it may be the patient. "durbalatvādanirharan" is printed as one word.

words.gloss: wind (vāta, flatus); stool; urine; obstruction, retention
basti (bladder, lower belly); navel; pain; ānāha (distension of the belly with retention)
heart; smearing, coating: hṛllepa (a "smearing" of the heart)

hindi: वायु, मल और मूत्र का अत्यन्त भयंकर विबन्ध यानी रुकावट करती है। बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय या निचले पेट और नाभि में पीड़ा, आनाह, हृदय का लेप और गुदा में सूजन।
english: Causes an extremely severe obstruction (vibandha) of wind (vāta), stool and urine. Pain in the basti (bladder, lower belly) and navel, ānāha (distension of the belly), hṛllepa (a "smearing" of the heart), and swelling in the anus.
notes:
line 05.06.8: Completes 5-7. "vāta" is read here as passing wind (flatus), the natural sense in the series wind, stool, urine; the Vāta humour is not meant to be excluded but the plain sense is taken. Modern equivalent: vibandha = constipation or retention (probable).
line 05.06.9: Elliptical: the verb karoti of 8 is carried over, none is supplied. "basti" in the first compound is the organ (bladder, lower belly) not the enema. Modern equivalents: ānāha = abdominal distension with obstruction (standard); hṛllepa = a coating or clinging sensation at the heart (probable); śvayathu = swelling (standard).

hindi: खुजली, गण्ड यानी गाँठें या सूजन, रंग का बिगड़ना, बेचैनी और अग्नि की मृदुता। पहले बताए गए दो काढ़े, मध्यम दोष में, अतिसार यानी दस्त वाले में।
english: Itching, gaṇḍa (lumps, swellings), discolouration, restlessness (arati) and softness (mārdava) of the fire (vahni). The pair of decoctions prescribed earlier, in a middling doṣa, in one with atisāra (diarrhoea).

text_flags.why: orthographic variant (nh for hn); normalised in words
possible: kvātha (decoction) with the v dropped; sense fits

notes:
line 05.06.10: Elliptical: the verb karoti of 8 is carried over, none is supplied. "vanhi" is the print's spelling of vahni (normalised, recorded here once). "gaṇḍa" has several senses (boil, swelling, also cheek); "lump, swelling" is taken. "vahni" is a name of the fire (agni); "softness of the fire" is kept literal, and probably points to weak digestion but this is not stated in the text.
line 05.06.11: GROUPING: 11 and 12 form one statement (11 names the pair, 12 says which one is drunk). "kāthadvayam" is read as kvātha-dvaya (the pair of decoctions): the print drops the v. "prāgvihita" refers to decoctions prescribed earlier in the book; which ones is not stated here. "atisārin" is read as the adjective "one having atisāra" (diarrhoea, standard). The pair is not identified.
OPEN (05.06.11) [minor] english / in a middling doṣa, in one with atisāra: madhyadoṣe and atisāriṇi are both locatives agreeing with the (unstated) patient; reading madhyadoṣe as a noun 'in a middling doṣa' next to 'in one with atisāra' gives two different referents. More natural: madhya-doṣa as a bahuvrīhi, 'in one with middling doṣa, with atisāra'. Suggested: Owner/human decision; suggested: 'in one with middling doṣa, with atisāra (diarrhoea)'; gram of madhya-doṣe then bahuvrīhi

hindi: इसलिए वहाँ एक, उष्ण का, पीना प्रशंसित है। फलवर्तियाँ, वैसे ही स्वेद, समय को जानकर विरेचन।
english: Therefore, in that case the drinking of one, the hot one, is recommended. Phalavartis (suppositories), likewise sweatings (sveda), and, having known the time, purgation (virecana).
notes:
line 05.06.12: GROUPING: continues 11. "tasmāt" is read as "therefore", with "ekasya" "of one" (of the two decoctions); the alternative "of that one" is possible. "uṣṇa" ("hot") is the choice made between the pair; whether the heat is of temperature or of potency is not stated. No noun is supplied in the translation.
line 05.06.13: Elliptical list; no verb in the unit and none is supplied. "phalavarti" is kept as the Sanskrit term (lit. "fruit-wick"); a medicated suppository is the standard sense. Which time is meant is not stated.

hindi: बिल्व यानी बेल की जड़, त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ, दारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु, यव, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी वाला। सुरा आदि और मूत्र वाली बस्ति, बिगड़े शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, उसे लाए।
english: Having bilva-root (wood-apple), trivṛt (turpeth), dāru (probably devadāru), yava (barley), kola (probably jujube) and kulattha (horse gram). The basti having surā and the others and urine, on a conjectural reading of the damaged word saprākūpeṣyaḥ, should bring it.
notes:
line 05.06.14: GROUPING: 14 and 15 form one statement; "-vān" ("having") here qualifies the basti named in 15. Identifications: bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard); trivṛt = Operculina turpethum (standard); dāru = devadāru, Cedrus deodara (probable; "dāru" alone is wood and is not secure); yava = barley, Hordeum vulgare (standard); kola = jujube fruit, Ziziphus jujuba (probable); kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard). Whether "bilvamūla" belongs inside the long compound (the print has a space) is not fixed.
line 05.06.15: The word "saprākūpeṣyas" is damaged or unintelligible in the print; no reading is built on it; the sense of the unit is therefore uncertain. "tam ānayet": the object tam is not stated, and what is "brought" is not stated. The half-line has 17 syllables (16 expected), which agrees with damage; the boundary of the damaged word is itself conjectural, so "tam ānayet" is also only a conjectural reading. "surādi" is read as "surā etc." (the series beginning with surā), kept literal.
OPEN (05.06.15) [minor] hindi / बिगड़े शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार: Awkward but faithful; English says 'should bring it' for tam ānayet although tam is only 'him/that (m.)'. Observation only. Suggested: owner may want 'bring him/that'

hindi: संशेष आम में, मृदु निरूह द्वारा, दोषों से प्रेरित। वायु को मूर्च्छित करता है, मार्ग को रोकता है और अग्नि को हानि पहुँचाता है।
english: In saṃśeṣa-āma (remaining āma), by a mild nirūha (decoction enema), stirred by the doṣas, It stupefies (mūrcchayati) the wind (anila), obstructs the path, and harms the fire (agni).
notes:
line 05.06.16: GROUPING: continues in 17 (verbs mūrcchayati, ruṇaddhi, hinasti). The reading of "saṃśeṣāme" is uncertain: saṃśeṣa-āma "remaining āma (undigested matter)" is taken, which is not secure; the subject of "īritaḥ" is taken to be the basti (nominative masculine) but is not named. The construction is elliptical. Reviewer: īritaḥ needs a masculine nominative subject; if the print has e for o, 'saṃśeṣāmo … īritaḥ' (the remaining āma, stirred by the doṣas, as subject of 17) would read more smoothly. Not adopted; no text_flag.
line 05.06.17: Continues 16 (subject not stated; "it" is the basti). "mūrcchayati" (lit. "makes swoon", also "thickens, congeals") is rendered "stupefies". The "path" and the "fire" are kept literal; the text does not say which path.

words.gloss: heaviness; fatigue; heart; pain; burning; bewilderment; veṣṭana: enveloping, twisting pain
drying, rough; sweating; digestive, promoting digestion (pācana)

hindi: भारीपन, थकान, हृदय में शूल, दाह, मोह और ऐंठन। तब करे; उसका रूक्ष, स्वेद और पाचन से उपचार करे।
english: Heaviness, fatigue, pain in the heart, burning, bewilderment and twisting (veṣṭana). Then one should do; one should treat him with drying (rūkṣa), sweating (sveda) and digestive (pācana) (ones).
notes:
line 05.06.18: GROUPING: continues 16-17 as the list of effects (verb carried over from the previous unit, none supplied). Modern equivalents: klama = fatigue, exhaustion (standard); saṃmoha = confusion, bewilderment (standard); veṣṭana = cramping, twisting pain (probable).
line 05.06.19: The verb "kuryāt" is left without an object; it is redundant beside "upacaret" and may be a mis-print or a remnant of another reading, but this is only a guess and is not applied. The instrumentals are neuter plural but no noun is stated. Follows the effects of 16-18 and begins the treatment, which continues in 20-25. 'rūkṣa-sveda-pācana' could also be read as rūkṣa-sveda ('dry fomentation') + pācana.

words.gloss: pippalī (long pepper, Piper longum; standard); kattṛṇa (a grass; identity disputed, sometimes the scented grass rauhiṣa, Cymbopogon; disputed); uśīra (vetiver, Vetiveria zizanioides; standard); dāru (probably devadāru, deodar, Cedrus deodara; probable; see 14); sūrvā (unidentified; possibly a variant of mūrvā, Marsdenia tenacissima, itself disputed); bhṛta: filled, borne
sauvarcala (a salt, black salt; standard); mixed
kindling (dīpana; a stimulant of the digestive fire)

hindi: पिप्पली यानी पीपर, कत्तृण यानी एक घास, उशीर यानी खस, दारु यानी सम्भवतः देवदारु और सूर्वा, जिसकी पहचान अनिश्चित है, से भरा जल। सौवर्चल यानी काले नमक से मिला, दीपन यानी अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करने वाला और हृदय में शोधन करने वाला जल पिए।
english: Water filled with pippalī (long pepper), kattṛṇa (a grass, identity uncertain), uśīra (vetiver), dāru (probably devadāru) and sūrvā (identity uncertain). One should drink it mixed with sauvarcala (black salt), kindling (dīpana) and cleansing in the heart.
notes:
line 05.06.20: GROUPING: continues in 21 (verb pibet). "bhṛta" (lit. "filled, borne") is rendered "filled with"; "prepared with, infused with" is the probable sense but is not stated. Identifications: pippalī = Piper longum (standard); kattṛṇa = a fragrant grass, perhaps rauhiṣa (Cymbopogon), disputed; uśīra = Vetiveria zizanioides (standard); sūrvā = mūrvā, Marsdenia tenacissima, disputed; the dāru as in line 05.06.14. Printed "kattṛṇa" is kept.
OPEN (05.06.20) [minor] text_flags / bhṛta: Observation, no patch: 'water … bhṛta' (filled with) is odd for a medicated water; 'śṛta' (boiled, i.e. made with the drugs) would be the usual word. Possible misprint; owner to decide whether to flag. Suggested: possible śṛtaṃ for bhṛtaṃ
line 05.06.21: Object "water" is carried from 20; the words dīpanam and hṛdiśodhanam are accusative singular neuter, read as agreeing with the water. Identification: sauvarcala = sochal or black salt (standard). "hṛdi-śodhana" is kept as "cleansing in the heart", the text gives no further detail.

words.gloss: vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus; standard); nāgara (dry ginger, Zingiber officinale; standard); śaṭhī (disputed; Hedychium spicatum or Curcuma zedoaria)
curd; maṇḍa (the watery or creamy part)

hindi: अथवा वचा यानी बच, नागर यानी सोंठ और शठी, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, दही के मण्ड से मिश्रित। पीने योग्य हों, प्रसन्ना से, या अरिष्ट से अथवा आसव से।
english: Or vacā (sweet flag), nāgara (dry ginger) and śaṭhī (identity disputed), mixed with curd-maṇḍa. They should be drunk with prasannā (a clear liquor), or with ariṣṭa or with āsava (fermented liquors).
notes:
line 05.06.22: GROUPING: continues 20-21, with 23 giving the vehicles (the sentence continues in 23). "mūrcchita" (lit. "swooned, thickened") is rendered "mixed" as a conjecture on the use for drugs; "prepared" is another possible sense. "dadhimaṇḍa" kept literal ("curd-maṇḍa"), the watery or creamy part of curd by standard use. Identifications: vacā = Acorus calamus (standard); nāgara = dry ginger (standard); śaṭhī = Hedychium spicatum or Curcuma zedoaria (disputed).
line 05.06.23: Completes 22. "prasannā" is read as the clear liquor (a kind of surā), the standard sense; "ariṣṭa" and "āsava" are two kinds of fermented liquor and are kept as terms.

hindi: और इसके लिए मूत्र सहित दशमूल वाली बस्ति दे। प्रयुक्त और अल्प वीर्य वाला, दोषों से भरे में, रूक्ष में, अथवा क्रूर आशय वाले में।
english: And one should administer to him a basti with urine, of the dāśamūla (the ten roots). Applied with little potency (vīrya), in one rich in doṣa, in a dry one, or in one with a harsh abode (āśaya).

text_flags.why: avagraha dropped in the print (yuktaḥ + alpa gives yukto 'lpa; same as śītolpa in line 05.06.6)

notes:
line 05.06.26: The members of the dāśamūla group are not listed in the text and are not listed here. "vidadhyāt" is rendered "should administer" (OPEN item in the glossary, similar verbs).
line 05.06.27: GROUPING: 27 and 28 form one statement (verb rundhyāt in 28). The subject basti is supplied only in 28. "yukta" is read as "applied" and "alpavīrya" as "of little potency"; "krūrāśaya" is kept literal ("harsh abode"); compare "krūrakoṣṭha" in 35. "yuktolpa" is yukto 'lpa with the avagraha dropped in the print, as in line 05.06.6 (flagged here and there). The verb is rundhyāt (28).

hindi: दोषों से ढकी हुई और रुके हुए मार्ग वाली बस्ति वायु को रोके। वह विपरीत मार्ग से गई वायु आध्मान और मर्म में पीड़ा करे।
english: The basti, covered by doṣa and with its path blocked, may obstruct the wind. That wind, gone the wrong way, would cause distension (ādhmāna) and oppression of the vital parts (marma).

text_flags.why: possible: spurious n; "doṣāvṛta" fits the sense and parallels line 05.06.36
possible: stray anusvara

notes:
line 05.06.28: Two print problems: "doṣānvṛto" is read as doṣa-āvṛtaḥ (compare 36, "āvṛto doṣaiḥ"), the spurious n being a probable mis-print; "ruddhamārgoṃ" has a stray anusvara. "samīraṇa" is a name of the wind. The subject "the basti" is the same as in 27.
line 05.06.29: Continues 28. "savimārgo" is read as sa vimārgaḥ ("that, gone the wrong way"); the alternative "sa-vimārga" (with a wrong path) is possible. "marma" are the vital parts or points of the body; kept as a term.

hindi: गुदा और कोष्ठ में जलन तथा अण्डकोष और वंक्षण में वेदना। हृदय को शूलों से रोकता है और इधर-उधर दौड़ता है।
english: Burning of the anus and koṣṭha (storehouse, belly), and pain in the testicles and groins. It obstructs the heart with pains, and runs here and there.
notes:
line 05.06.30: Elliptical: verb "kuryāt" of 29 is carried over, none is supplied. "gudakoṣṭha" may be read as the koṣṭha of the anus; "anus and koṣṭha" is taken. "muṣka" = testicle (also scrotum).
line 05.06.31: The subject is not stated; the wind (anila) of 29 is understood, but it is only supplied as "it". "itaścetaśca" = itaḥ ca itaḥ ca, "here and there".

words.gloss: pīlu (toothbrush tree, Salvadora persica; probable); sarṣapa (mustard, Brassica juncea; probable); urine; having

hindi: उसमें, जिसका शरीर भली-भाँति अभ्यक्त और स्वेदित है, वर्ति का प्रयोग करे। और बिल्व आदि वाला निरूह पीलु यानी सम्भवतः जाल, सर्षप यानी सम्भवतः सरसों और मूत्र वाला हो।
english: In that case, to one whose body is well anointed and sweated, one should apply a varti (suppository). And the nirūha (a decoction enema) beginning with bilva should have pīlu (probably the toothbrush tree), sarṣapa (probably mustard) and urine.

text_flags.why: orthographic doubling of t; normalised in words
orthographic variant (v for b); normalised in words

notes:
line 05.06.32: The print writes "varttim" with doubled t, normalised to varti in words (recorded once). "varti" is kept as a term (a wick-shaped suppository). The unit says "of one whose body ..." (genitive) and "applies a varti"; the direction of application is not stated and is not added.
line 05.06.33: The print writes "vilva" for bilva (orthographic, normalised, recorded once). The members of the bilva group are not listed. "nirūha" is kept as a term (a decoction enema; standard). Identifications: pīlu = Salvadora persica (probable); sarṣapa = mustard, probably Brassica juncea (probable).

hindi: और अनुवासन, अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार जिसका पहला भाग सरला है उस बिगड़े शब्द से सिद्ध किया हुआ। बहुत दोष और बल वाले में तथा क्रूर कोष्ठ वाले में बस्ति पतली और मृदु,
english: And an anuvāsana (oil enema) prepared with the damaged word saralāmadaruibhyām, on a conjectural reading beginning with sarala. In one with much doṣa and strength, with a harsh koṣṭha (storehouse, belly), a basti thin and mild,

text_flags.why: possible: damaged print (displaced i-sign); a guess from the ending -bhyām and the usual pairing, not adopted. Closer in letters: saralāmaradārubhyāṃ (sarala + amaradāru; amaradāru is a synonym of devadāru); saralādevadārubhyāṃ is a further alternative
proofread pass (stray, error): stray i-matra and chandrabindu
possible: stray candrabindu in the print (shown as ~ in the transliteration)

notes:
line 05.06.34: The word "saralāmadaruibhyāṃ" is damaged in the print (a displaced i-sign); the ending -bhyām suggests an instrumental dual ("with the two"), and the beginning looks like saralā (sarala, chir pine, Pinus roxburghii, probable), but the rest is unclear and no reading is built on it; a possible original is "saralā-devadārubhyām" (with sarala and devadāru), a guess only. Printed word kept unsplit.
line 05.06.35: GROUPING: 35 and 36 form one statement (verb pratihanti in 36). The print has a tilde in "bahu~doṣabale", taken as a mis-print; the reading "much doṣa and strength" is kept but not secure (bala could also be "strong").

words.gram: pres. part. anu-√sṛ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: ठंडी, अल्प और दोषों से ढकी हुई वह वायु को रोकती है। ऊपर की ओर शरीर में चलती हुई वह वायु सिर की पीड़ा करे।
english: Cold, small and covered by the doṣas, it obstructs the wind. That wind (vāyu), moving upward along the body, would cause head-pain (headache).
notes:
line 05.06.36: The subject is the basti of 35 ("it"). Print forms: "śīto'lpaścāvṛto" = śītaḥ alpaḥ ca āvṛtaḥ.
line 05.06.37: Continues 36. Modern equivalent: śiroruj = headache (standard).

words.gloss: hot; oil; salt; smeared; sweated; pressed, kneaded

hindi: गर्दन की जकड़न, प्रतिश्याय यानी जुकाम, बहरापन और दृष्टि का भ्रम। उसे, जिस पर गर्म तेल और नमक लगाया गया है, जो स्वेदित और मर्दित है।
english: Stiffness of the neck, pratiśyāya (nasal catarrh), deafness and disturbance of vision. Him, smeared with hot oil and salt, sweated and kneaded.
notes:
line 05.06.38: Elliptical: the verb "kuryāt" of 37 is carried over, none is supplied. Modern equivalents: pratiśyāya = coryza, nasal catarrh (standard); dṛṣṭivibhrama = disturbed or confused vision (standard).
line 05.06.39: GROUPING: 39, 40 and 41 form one statement (verb yojayet in 41, object tam). "mardita" (lit. "ground, crushed") is rendered "kneaded"; massaged is also possible.

words.gloss: with pradhamana (blowing of powder into the nose)

hindi: तीक्ष्ण धूमों, प्रधमन, नस्य और आस्य-विरेचनों से। विरेचनों और बस्तियों से, जो आनुलोमिक यानी स्वाभाविक दिशा के अनुसार हैं, शीघ्र उसका उपचार करे।
english: With sharp smokes, with pradhamana (powder-blowing), nasya (nasal medicines), and mouth-purgings (āsyavirecana), With purgations and bastis, quickly, one should treat (him) with ānulomika (following the natural direction) (ones).
notes:
line 05.06.40: Continues 39 (verb in 41). "dhūma" is smoke (inhaled smoke); "pradhamana" and "nasya" are kept as terms. "āsyavirecana" is kept literal ("mouth-evacuation"); what exactly is evacuated is not stated.
line 05.06.41: Completes 39-40; the object "him" is carried from 39. "ānulomika" means "following the natural (downward) direction"; kept literal. Which of the preceding instrumentals it qualifies is not fixed by the grammar.

words.gram: m. acc. sg., agrees with doṣam

hindi: स्निग्ध और स्वेदित में, महान् दोष होने पर, मृदु और अल्प औषध वाली बस्ति दोष को उभारकर थोड़ा दोष निकालेगी और प्रवाहिका यानी पेचिश उत्पन्न करेगी।
english: In (one) who is oiled and sweated, when the doṣa is great, a basti (enema) that is mild and has little drug. Having stirred up the doṣa, (it) would remove a little doṣa and would produce pravāhikā (dysentery with straining).

text_flags.why: possible: 'utklaiśya' is not a regular form; the gerund of ut-√kliś (causative) is 'utkleśya'; 'ai' is probably a printing slip for 'e' (metre unchanged)

notes:
line 05.06.42: GROUPING: lines 05.06.42-45 read as one statement about a mild basti with little drug: 42 gives the conditions, the verbs are in 43 (haret, janayet), and 44-45 give the signs. The subject basti is carried to 43 and no verb is supplied here. 'snigdhasvinne' is taken as a locative 'in (one) oiled and sweated'; it could also be read as a locative absolute with 'mahādoṣe'. 'mṛdu' and 'alpabheṣaja' are taken as two adjectives of the basti.
line 05.06.43: Continues 42 (subject basti, 'it'). Modern equivalent: pravāhikā = dysentery with painful straining at stool (standard). 'alpam' agrees with 'doṣam' (a little doṣa).

hindi: बस्ति और अपान में शोफ यानी सूजन, और जाँघों तथा पिंडलियों में सदन यानी शिथिलता। जिसकी वायु रुकी हुई है, वह प्राणी बार-बार जोर लगाता है।
english: Swelling (śopha) in the basti (bladder, lower belly) and in the apāna (anus), and sinking (sadana, weakness) in the thighs and shanks. The being (jantu) whose wind is obstructed strains repeatedly.

text_flags.why: possible: 'bhīkṣṇa' is not a word; the initial a of 'abhīkṣṇam' (repeatedly) seems lost; this fits the sense and gives the 16 syllables of the half-verse

notes:
line 05.06.44: Elliptical: the verb 'janayet' of 43 is carried over and none is supplied. 'basti' here is the organ (bladder, lower belly), not the enema. 'apāna' is taken as the anal region; the other sense, the downward wind (apāna), is possible. Modern equivalents: śopha = swelling, oedema (standard); sadana = sinking, lassitude, weakness (standard).
line 05.06.45: Appears to complete the statement of 42-45. 'pravāhate' is the verb that gives pravāhikā its name: straining, as at stool. 'jantu' is a being, a creature; it is kept literal.

hindi: स्वेदन, अभ्यंग और निरूह, शोधनीय यानी शोधन करने वाले और अनुलोमिक यानी स्वाभाविक दिशा के अनुसार, विधान करे; और लंघन यानी उपवास कराकर उसकी वृत्ति यानी आचरण विरेचन किए हुए के समान रखे।
english: Sweatings (sveda), anointings (abhyaṅga) and nirūhas (decoction enemas), cleansing (śodhanīya) and ānulomika (following the natural direction) (ones), One should prescribe, and, having subjected (him) to laṅghana (lightening, fasting), (prescribe) his regimen (vṛtti) like that of one purged.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed word has no ending for 'vṛtti' as the object of 'vidadhyāt'; 'vṛttiṃ tasya' (his regimen) fits the sense and the 16 syllables; 'vṛttis tasya' (nominative, verb understood) is the other possibility

notes:
line 05.06.46: GROUPING: 46 and 47 form one statement (verb vidadhyāt in 47), and follow 42-45. The adjectives 'śodhanīyānulomikān' agree with all three accusatives (all masculine); whether they qualify only the nirūhas is not decided. The printed 'śodhanīyānulomikān' may be śodhanīya-ānulomikān (as read) or śodhanīya-anulomikān; ānulomika is kept as in the earlier chunk.
line 05.06.47: Appears to complete 46. 'viriktavat' is 'as for one who has been purged'. 'laṅghana' is kept as a term (lightening by fasting). The second 'prescribe' is implied by the accusative 'vṛttim'; the reading rests on the possible correction in text_flags.
OPEN (05.06.47) [minor] hindi / वृत्ति यानी आचरण ... रखे: "आचरण" is an interpretation of vṛtti and "रखे" is a supplied verb; the whole second half rests on the conjectural vṛttiṃ tasya. Owner to decide whether to word it more literally (e.g. "उसकी वृत्ति विरेचित के समान") and whether the English should bracket the supplied "(prescribe)" as a conjecture, which it does; Hindi cannot use brackets. Suggested: human decision

words.gram: bahuvrīhi (a- governing all), m. nom. sg.

hindi: वेग का संरोध यानी रोकना करता हुआ, अथवा अतिमात्रा से पीड़ित, अथवा अस्निग्ध, नमक और गर्मी से रहित, अल्प और अल्प औषध वाली बस्ति,
english: Causing holding back (saṃrodha) of the urge (vega), or pressed by excess quantity, Or a basti lacking unctuousness, salt (lavaṇa) and heat, small, with little drug,

text_flags.why: possible: the print has a stray tilde (ku~r) and the plural 'kurvanto' does not agree with the singular basti of 49; 'kurvan' is expected, but 'kurvanto' fits the 16 syllables, so this is only suspected
possible: 'agnigdha' is not a word; 'asnigdha' (not unctuous) is the likely word, 's' and 'g' being easily confused in the print

notes:
line 05.06.48: GROUPING: 48-51 form one statement about a basti that is thrown upward; the subject is the basti named in 49 ('bastiḥ'), the verb 'nireti' is in 51. Subject and sense of 'pīḍita' are not stated: 'pressed, squeezed' (the basti pressed by excess quantity) is taken; 'afflicted' (the patient) is the other possibility. 'vegasaṃrodha' is the holding back of a natural urge; which urge is not stated.
OPEN (05.06.48) [minor] text_flags / ku~rvaṃto -> kurvan: Weak flag, and the draft is internally inconsistent: the printed form kurvanto gives the 16 syllables (the print has a stray candrabindu, कुँर्वंतो), while the correction kurvan gives 14 and breaks the metre, yet `words` already uses kurvan. Metre favours keeping kurvanto (nom. pl.), which then disagrees with the singular subject basti; an alternative is that the subject is not the basti. Owner to decide between w=kurvan (grammar) and w=kurvantaḥ (metre); either way keep the flag as "possible". Suggested: human decision
OPEN (05.06.48) [minor] hindi / करता हुआ ... पीड़ित: Gender/sense: बस्ति is feminine in the other Hindi lines (निकालेगी, करती), and "पीड़ित" reads as "afflicted" while the English says "pressed" (notes keep both open). Suggested: human decision
line 05.06.49: Continues 48. The compound is read with a- governing all three members (without unctuousness, salt and heat), as in the list of 'little oil, salt, drug' defects of chapter line 05.06.6; the alternative is only snigdha negated ('not unctuous, (but) salty and hot'). The reading is not firm.

words.gloss: fainting; nausea; thirst; burning; and others

words.gram: pres. part. pra-√vṛt caus., m. nom. sg.

hindi: अथवा मृदु, वायु द्वारा ऊपर की ओर फेंकी गई, मुख और नासिका से, बाहर निकलती है, मूर्च्छा, हृल्लास यानी मिचली, प्यास, दाह आदि को उत्पन्न करती हुई।
english: Or mild, thrown upward by the wind, from the mouth and nose, (It) comes out, producing fainting (mūrcchā), nausea (hṛllāsa), thirst, burning (dāha) and the others.

text_flags.why: possible: the extra 'a' in 'tṛḍadāha' breaks the sandhi of tṛṭ + dāha (tṛḍdāha) and makes the half-verse 17 instead of 16 syllables

notes:
line 05.06.50: Continues 48-49; the verb 'nireti' is in 51, and the subject is the basti of 49.
line 05.06.51: Appears to complete 48-51. The print writes 'pravarttayan' with doubled t, normalised to 'pravartayan' (recorded once for the chunk). Modern equivalents: mūrcchā = fainting, swoon (standard); hṛllāsa = nausea (standard); dāha = burning sensation (standard).

hindi: उसकी मूर्च्छा के विकार को देखकर शीतल जल से मुख को सींचे। आक्लम यानी थकावट के नाश तक पंखा झले और प्राणायाम कराए।
english: Having seen his disorder (vikāra) of fainting, one should sprinkle the face with cold water. One should fan (him) until the destruction of the exhaustion (āklama), and should make (him) do prāṇāyāma (breath control).
notes:
line 05.06.52: 'asya' is taken as 'his', going with the fainting and the face.
line 05.06.53: 'vyajet' is read as 'should fan' (from vyajana, a fan; probable, the verb is rare). 'āklamanāśāt' is an ablative, here 'up to the destruction of exhaustion'. The person fanned is not named.
OPEN (05.06.53) [minor] split / āklama-nāśāt: Probably two words: ā (up to) + klama-nāśāt (ablative, "until the destruction of fatigue"); a noun āklama is doubtful, and the printed व्यजेदाक्लमनाशाच्च reads naturally as vyajet ā klamanāśāt ca. English/Hindi "(āklama)" / "आक्लम यानी" would then go. Cannot be patched (one word becomes two). Suggested: split ā + klama-nāśāt; English "until the destruction of fatigue (klama)"
OPEN (05.06.53) [minor] gram / vyajet: Analysis as a denominative of vyajana looks wrong: vyajet is simply the potential of vi-√aj (to fan, drive), the source of the noun vyajana. Sense unchanged. Suggested: 3 sg. pot. vi-√aj; notes: not a denominative

hindi: पीठ, पार्श्व और उदर को गर्म हाथों से मसले, मुख नीचे की ओर करके। बालों में खींचकर हिलाए और व्याल यानी सर्प या हिंसक पशुओं तथा दाढ़ वालों से डराए।
english: One should knead the back, sides and belly with hot hands, (him) face downward. Having pulled (him) by the hair, one should shake (him) and frighten (him) with vyāla (snakes or savage beasts) and fanged (ones).
notes:
line 05.06.54: The person is not named. 'adhomukham' is taken as describing the person (face downward); it cannot agree with the neuter 'udaram' in a sensible way. Continues the treatment of the fainting in 52-53.
line 05.06.55: The print writes 'vyāḻa' with ḻ; normalised to 'vyāla' (recorded once for the chunk; the same ḻ appears for l elsewhere in the print). 'vyāla' is a snake or a savage beast; 'daṃṣṭrin' is a fanged or tusked animal; the compound is read as a pair. Continues 52-54 (the person is not named).

hindi: शस्त्रों, उल्का यानी जलती लकड़ी और राजपुरुषों से; क्योंकि इस प्रकार बस्ति नीचे जाती है। और हाथों तथा वस्त्रों से गले का आपीड़ यानी दबाव करे, मानो वह मर रहा हो।
english: With weapons, firebrands (ulkā) and the king's men (rāja-puruṣa); for thus the basti goes downward. And one should make pressure (āpīḍa) on the throat with the hands and cloths, as if he were dying.
notes:
line 05.06.56: Continues 55 (verb bhīṣayet). 'ulkā' is a firebrand or torch (it also means meteor). 'rāja-puruṣa' is a king's man, an officer or soldier.
line 05.06.57: 'mriyate yathā' is taken as 'as if he were dying'; 'in such a way that he dies' is the literal sense and is not intended. Continues 55-56.

hindi: क्योंकि प्राण और उदान के निरोध से, जिसका मार्ग और अधिक भली-भाँति स्थापित हो गया है, अपान वायु उस बस्ति को शीघ्र ही खींच लेती है।
english: For, from the obstruction of prāṇa and udāna, (the one) whose course is the more fully established, The apāna wind (pavana) quickly draws that basti away.
notes:
line 05.06.58: GROUPING: 58 and 59 form one statement: the bahuvrīhi 'suprasiddhatarāyaṇaḥ' (masculine) agrees with 'apānaḥ pavanaḥ' of 59. The sense of 'suprasiddha' ('well established') is literal; the context suggests that the course of apāna, the downward wind, is freed, but this is an interpretation (probable) and is not put in the translation. Sandhi: -tara + ayana gives -tarāyaṇa (ṇ after r).
line 05.06.59: Appears to complete 58. 'apakarṣati' means draws off or draws away; the prefix apa- does not itself say 'down', and 'down' is not added.

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus; standard); kramuka (areca nut, Areca catechu; probable); paste (kalka)
would bring into the natural direction

hindi: और कुष्ठ यानी कूठ तथा क्रमुक यानी सम्भवतः सुपारी का कल्क यानी पिसी लुगदी, अम्ल से युक्त, पिलाए। उष्णता, तीक्ष्णता और सरत्व के कारण वह भी बस्ति को स्वाभाविक दिशा में ले आता है।

english: In (one) with a soft koṣṭha (belly), in the weak (one), a basti (enema) that is very sharp and over-expelling, (it) would cause hiccup (hidhmā). In that (case), whatever is hiccup-destroying and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) is beneficial.

possible: 'pakvā' for paktvā (t lost; gerund of √pac); alternative: 'pakvam' agreeing with tailam, same sense

english: He should give (it) smeared (mixed) with hot water and with pippalī (long pepper), joined with salt. With smoke (dhūma), linctus (leha), juice (rasa), milk and fomentation (sveda), and also food that drives away Vāta.
notes:
line 05.06.90: The object of 'dadyāt' is not stated; 'aktam' and 'saṃyutam' are neuter accusatives agreeing with an unstated neuter noun (probably the oil or enema of 89), not applied.

words.gloss: kāśa (Saccharum spontaneum; standard); kuśa (Desmostachya bipinnata; standard); utkaṭa (unclear here: 'excessive, strong', or a drug name)

english: (A basti) that is very sharp, or with vāta (wind, air), or not properly pressed, The basti (enema) would strike the heart. In that (case), with kāśa (Saccharum spontaneum), kuśa (Desmostachya bipinnata) and utkaṭa (unclear),
notes:
line 05.06.92: GROUPING: 92 and 93 appear to be one sentence; the subject 'bastiḥ' is in 93. 'savāta' may mean 'with air (in the bag or syringe)' or 'with Vāta (the humour)'; the text does not say; both are possible.
line 05.06.93: GROUPING: 93 to 95 read as one passage. 'utkaṭa' is unclear: it may be an adjective ('strong, excessive') or a drug name; no reading is applied and no identification is made. The sentence continues in 94 and 95.

words.gloss: together with; sour (ones); salt; skandha (trunk, stem; what is meant is unclear); karīra (bamboo shoot or Capparis decidua; disputed); badarī (jujube, Ziziphus jujuba; standard); fruits

hindi: सहित खट्टे, नमक, स्कन्ध यानी तना, जिसका आशय यहाँ अस्पष्ट है, करीर यानी बाँस का अंकुर या कैर और बदरी यानी बेर के फलों के साथ हो। उबाले हुओं से बस्ति हितकारी है, पकाया हुआ, और वात को नष्ट करने वाले अनुवासनों से।
english: It would be with sour (ones), salt, skandha (trunk; unclear here), karīra (disputed: bamboo shoot, or the shrub Capparis decidua) and badarī (jujube) fruits, A basti with boiled (ones) is beneficial, siddha (cooked), and with Vāta-destroying anuvāsanas (oil enemas).
notes:
line 05.06.94: GROUPING: appears to continue 93 and leads into 95 ('śṛtaiḥ'). The grouping of the compound is uncertain: 'sāmla' may attach only to 'lavaṇa' (with sour and salt), and 'skandha' may be a plant part rather than a drug. 'karīra' is disputed (bamboo shoot, or the thorny shrub Capparis decidua).
line 05.06.95: GROUPING: appears to end the passage of 93 to 95. The syntax is loose: 'siddhaḥ' may mean 'cooked', 'accomplished' or 'effective', and 'vātaghnaiś cānuvāsanaiḥ' may belong with 'siddhaḥ' or be a second means; the translation keeps the order of the Sanskrit.

hindi: कोमल कोष्ठ वाले और अल्प दोष वाले के लिए, रूखी, तीक्ष्ण और अत्यधिक मात्रा वाली बस्ति के मलों को शीघ्र नष्ट करके वात और पित्त को कुपित कर दे।
english: For (one) with a soft koṣṭha (belly) and little doṣa, (a basti that is) dry, sharp and excessive in quantity, having quickly destroyed the malas (wastes) of the basti, would aggravate Vāta and Pitta.
notes:
line 05.06.96: GROUPING: 96 to 98 appear to be one sentence; the subject (a basti) is understood from the context and the verb 'prakopayet' is in 97. 'atimātraka' is read 'exceeding the measure, excessive in quantity'. 'mṛdukoṣṭhālpadoṣasya' is read as one bahuvrīhi (soft koṣṭha, little doṣa), or as two genitives.
line 05.06.97: GROUPING: appears to continue 96. 'bastimalān' is printed with ḻ (ळ); read as mala. 'basti' can mean the enema or the bladder, and 98 lists 'basti' beside the navel and the anus, so 'bastimala' may be the wastes of the basti region or of the bladder; the translation keeps the word basti.
OPEN (05.06.97) [minor] notes / bastimaḻān: ळ is printed for ल; the word list uses l without a flag. Likely a print habit of this Marathi-printed edition; record once book-wide as orthographic normalisation (see glossary_suggestions). Suggested: no patch

hindi: वे तो इसकी नाभि, बस्ति और गुदा को बार-बार काटते हुए अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, विवर्ण यानी रंग का बिगड़ना, थोड़ा थोड़ा उत्थान यानी उठना; बस्ति निर्लेखन यानी खुरचने वाली हो।
english: They, indeed, cutting his navel, basti (probably the bladder) and anus again and again, On a conjectural reading: discolouration, a little-by-little arising (utthāna); the basti would be scraping (nirlekhana).

hindi: चिपचिपी बस्ति हितकारी है, और मीठों के साथ उबाला हुआ स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा। क्षार, खट्टी, तीक्ष्ण, गर्म और नमकीन बस्ति, या पित्त वाले की
english: A slimy (picchila) basti is beneficial, and a sneha (oil or fat) boiled with sweet (ones). A basti (enema) that is kṣāra, sour, sharp, hot and salty, or (that) of (one) who is paittika (of Pitta),
notes:

lines_deva: सविदग्धं स्त्रवत्यस्रं वर्णैः पित्तं च भूरिशः
lines_iast: savidagdhaṃ stravatyasraṃ varṇaiḥ pittaṃ ca bhūriśaḥ
hindi: गुदा को जलाते, खुरचते और क्षति पहुँचाते हुए यह इसके लिए परिस्रव यानी बहाव कर देता है। जलने सहित रक्त बहता है, रंगों के साथ, और पित्त बहुत मात्रा में भी।
english: Burning, scraping and damaging the anus, it makes a flow (parisrava) for him. It discharges blood together with the burnt (vidagdha), with colours, and Pitta, abundantly.
notes:
line 05.06.106: GROUPING: appears to continue 105 (subject: the basti of 105). 'kṣiṇvan' (printed) is read as the present participle of √kṣi, 'damaging, wasting'; the exact sense is not certain.
line 05.06.107: GROUPING: appears to continue 106. 'savidagdham' is read with 'asram' (blood together with what is burnt); 'vidagdha' is not specified further (it can mean scorched, over-heated). 'varṇaiḥ' is plural, 'with colours'. Raktapitta-like bleeding is not named here. The reading is literal.
OPEN (05.06.107) [minor] hindi / जलने सहित: savidagdham is rendered 'with the burnt' in English but 'with burning' in Hindi; the parse (adjective of asram, or an adverb/noun) is undecided and the two languages should follow one reading. Left for the owner. Suggested: none

english: And many times, with excessive urge (vega), (he) goes into moha (bewilderment, fainting), repeatedly. In that (case), on a conjectural reading: goat's milk boiled with crushed, fresh śāmalī (probably śālmalī, the silk-cotton tree) tantra (threads, fibres; unclear),

line 05.06.108: GROUPING: appears to end the passage 105 to 108. The subject of 'gacchati' (the patient) is not named. 'moha' is rendered bewilderment or fainting; the text gives only the word moha. Modern equivalent: fainting or loss of awareness (probable).

'śāmalī' is not a known word; śālmalī (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; probable) is likely, with the l-m conjunct lost. 'tantra' (thread, fibre) as a plant part is unclear and is not enriched. english: Strained, joined with ghee, he should give a basti (enema), and other slimy (ones). Thus is the kalpa (preparation) in the sprouts of vaṭa (banyan) and the rest, and in yava (barley) and tila (sesame).

line 05.06.110: GROUPING: appears to complete 109. The participles 'pūtam' and 'ghṛtānvitam' are neuter and agree with the milk (payaḥ) of 109. 'anyān ca picchilān' is read as other slimy (bastis); the noun is not stated, so 'bastis' is not added to the translation.

'evam kalpaḥ' is read as 'the preparation is thus', that is, as in 109 and 110; this is an inference from the context.

Alternative to the flag: the space in 'seka pralepanān' may be spurious, giving one compound sekapralepanān (pourings and coatings); the sense is the same.

words.gloss: rakta-pitta (raktapitta: a bleeding disorder, bleeding from the body openings; standard); atisāra (diarrhoea; standard); destroying

hindi: और यहाँ रक्तपित्त यानी रक्तस्राव का रोग तथा अतिसार यानी दस्त को नष्ट करने वाली क्रिया प्रशंसित है। दाह आदि में त्रिवृत् यानी निशोथ का कल्क मृद्वीका यानी अंगूर के जल से पिए।
english: And here, the procedure (kriyā) that destroys raktapitta (a bleeding disorder) and atisāra (diarrhoea) is commended. In dāha (burning) and the rest, he should drink a paste (kalka) of trivṛt (turpeth) with mṛdvīkā water (grape water).
notes:
line 05.06.114: The line is read as a single statement, 'the procedure that destroys raktapitta and atisāra is commended here'. Raktapitta is kept as the Sanskrit name; the modern equivalent given is a descriptive one (a disorder with bleeding), not a single named disease.
line 05.06.115: 'mṛdvīkāvāriṇā' is read as 'with the water of mṛdvīkā (grape)'; whether this means raisin water, grape juice or an infusion is not stated. 'dāhādiṣu' means dāha and the rest; the other members are not named.

hindi: वह तो पित्त, मल और वात को नष्ट करके दाह आदि को जीत लेता है। और शुद्ध होकर शर्करा यानी चीनी से युक्त ठण्डी यवागू यानी पतली लपसी पिए।
english: That, indeed, having destroyed Pitta, faeces and Vāta, would conquer (those) beginning with burning (dāha). And, purified, he should drink a cool yavāgū (thin gruel) joined with sugar (śarkarā).
notes:
line 05.06.116: GROUPING: appears to explain 115. 'pittaśakṛdvātān' is a dvandva in the masculine accusative plural (the final member vāta is masculine; pitta is neuter). 'hatvā' is literally 'having killed'; here 'having destroyed'. It is possible that 'destroyed' means 'expelled', but the text says only hatvā.
line 05.06.117: 'viśuddhaḥ' is 'purified' (the purging is understood from the context). 'śarkarā' is read as sugar, not gravel.

words.gloss: māṣa (black gram, Vigna mungo; standard); soup (yūṣa)
kulmāṣa (a preparation of partly cooked grain; probable)

hindi: अथवा अत्यधिक विरेचन किए हुए और क्षीण मल वाले के लिए भोजन का प्रयोग करे। माष यानी उड़द के यूष के साथ कुल्माष यानी सम्भवतः अधपका अन्न; पीने के लिए दही अथवा सुरा यानी एक नशीला पेय।
english: Or he should employ food for (one) who is over-purged (and) whose stool is depleted. Kulmāṣa (probably a preparation of partly cooked grain) with māṣa (black gram) soup (yūṣa); as drink, curd or else surā (an intoxicating drink).
notes:
line 05.06.118: 'yuñjyāt' is read 'should employ'. The run-on 'ativiriktasyakṣīṇaviṭkasya' is read as two genitives (or one compound); the sense is the same. The two members are of the same person.
line 05.06.119: GROUPING: appears to continue 118 ('bhojanam'). Kulmāṣa is read as a preparation of partly cooked grain (probable); the exact sense differs between authors. The verb 'yuñjyāt' is carried over from 118 and is not supplied.

words.gloss: would pass (lit. would be made to sit [to evacuate])
ghana (probably musta, nut-grass, Cyperus rotundus; probable; lit. 'cloud')
kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus; standard; here a drug name)
unclear (printed 'nadāru'; not a known drug name; possibly a damaged 'dāru')

hindi: जो पीड़ा वाला, अरुचि सहित, कच्चा और सड़ा हुआ त्याग करे अनुमानित पाठ के अनुसार, घन यानी सम्भवतः नागरमोथा, अतिविषा यानी अतीस, कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, नदारु, जिसका अर्थ अस्पष्ट है, और वचा यानी बच के साथ पिए।
english: He who, in pain and with aruci (distaste for food), would pass raw, putrid (kuṇapa) (ones), On a conjectural reading: he should drink (them) together with ghana (probably musta), ativiṣā (Aconitum heterophyllum), kuṣṭha (costus), nadāru (unclear) and vacā (sweet flag).

text_flags.why: possible: 'nadāru' is unknown; a stray 'na' (or a damaged 'dāru') is suspected; not applied

notes:
line 05.06.120: GROUPING: 120 to 122 appear to be one sentence (the treatment is in 121). 'upaveśyeta' (to go to stool) is read as passing; the noun it governs is not stated, so the English supplies only '(ones)'; the Hindi keeps only the adjectives. 'kuṇapa' is rendered putrid (foul-smelling); the lexical sense is corpse.
OPEN (05.06.120) [minor] gram / upaveśyeta: Gram says passive causative ('would be made to sit/evacuate') but English and Hindi use an active 'would pass'. Owner to decide the rendering. Suggested: none
line 05.06.121: GROUPING: appears to complete 120. The compound is a dvandva with 'sa' (together with). 'nadāru' is not a known drug name; it may be a damaged 'dāru' (or a stray 'na' before it); no reading is applied. Which preparation is drunk (powder, decoction) is not stated. 'kuṣṭha' here is the drug, not the disease.
OPEN (05.06.121) [minor] text_flags / nadāru: Second possible repair not recorded: 'nadāru' may be 'nata-dāru' (nata = tagara; ta/na confusion), giving kuṣṭha, nata, dāru, vacā. Not applied. Suggested: mention as alternative in notes

lines_deva: पक्वं तत्र स्ववर्गीयो बस्तिः श्रेष्ठं भिषग्जितं
lines_iast: pakvaṃ tatra svavargīyo bastiḥ śreṣṭhaṃ bhiṣagjitaṃ

words.gloss: is made to flow out (is purged)

hindi: जिसके मल, वात, रक्त, पित्त अथवा कफ का अतिसरण कराया जाता है, पक्व; वहाँ अपने वर्ग का बस्ति श्रेष्ठ है, वैद्य के द्वारा जीता गया।
english: (He) who is made to flow out faeces, Vāta, blood, Pitta or Kapha, Cooked (pakva); in that (case), a basti of its own group (svavargīya) is best, (what is) conquered by the physician (bhiṣagjita).

text_flags.why: possible: 'q' for kṛ and 't' for s in 'matṛk' (asṛk); the sense (faeces, Vāta, blood, Pitta) fits

notes:
line 05.06.122: GROUPING: appears to complete 120 and 121 as a list of what flows out; the treatment continues in 123. The print is corrupt: see text_flags; the intended words are read as śakṛt, vātam, asṛk, pittam. The Hindi keeps the sense 'whose ... is made to flow out'.
OPEN (05.06.122) [minor] gram / atisāryate: 'ati-' may mean 'excessively' (cf. ativiriktasya, 118); English 'made to flow out' drops it. Open; owner. Suggested: none
line 05.06.123: GROUPING: unclear; 'pakvam' may belong to the end of 122 or begin a new statement, and the unit may continue in the next chunk. 'pakvam' (cooked or ripe) has no stated noun and no sense is applied. 'svavargīya' is 'belonging to its own group' (the group of drugs for the same condition is not stated). 'bhiṣagjitam' is read 'conquered by the physician' (the alternative is 'the physician's victory'); the neuter 'śreṣṭham' with the masculine 'bastiḥ' is also loose. Possible link with the next chunk: line 05.06.124 begins 'ṣaṇṇām eṣām dvisaṃsargāt triṃśad bhedāḥ' (of these six, thirty by pairing); line 05.06.122 lists five items (śakṛt, vāta, asṛk, pitta, kapha), so 'pakvam' may be a sixth item of that list. This is an inference, not a decision.

hindi: इन छह के दो-दो के संयोग से तीस भेद होते हैं। अकेलों के साथ छत्तीस को जाने, उपद्रवों सहित भी।
english: Of these six, from the combination of two, there are thirty varieties. Together with the single (ones), one should know thirty-six, also with their complications (upadrava).
notes:
line 05.06.124: The six are not named in this unit. Thirty is as printed; the text does not explain how the count is reached (it is not the number of pairs of six). 'triṃśadbhedā bhavanti' is regular sandhi (āḥ before b becomes ā).
OPEN (05.06.124) [minor] notes / triṃśad-bhedāḥ: Count: 6 items give 15 pairs, yet the print says 30. Not a typo to correct: 125 says 36 "together with the single ones" = 30 + 6, so the book is internally consistent. Keep "thirty" as printed; the draft note is right not to correct it. Suggested: (owner decision; no machine patch)
line 05.06.125: The noun for the thirty-six is not stated; no noun is added. Thirty-six equals the thirty of 124 plus six, but the text does not say so. 'kevalaiḥ' read as 'single, alone'; 'sa-upadravān' is accusative plural, agreeing with the unstated object of vidyāt. GROUPING: 125 appears to follow on 124 and 126-127 name the upadravas.

words.gloss: pain; pravāhikā (straining at stool, tenesmus; standard); distension; cutting pain; loss of appetite; fevers
thirst; bewilderment; burning; fainting; and so on

hindi: शूल यानी पीड़ा, प्रवाहिका यानी मल के लिए ज़ोर लगना, आध्मान यानी अफारा, परिकर्ती यानी काटने की पीड़ा, अरुचि यानी भोजन की अनिच्छा और ज्वर यानी बुखार। तृष्णा यानी प्यास, मोह यानी भ्रम, दाह यानी जलन, मूर्च्छा यानी बेहोशी आदि को भी इनके उपद्रव जाने।
english: Pain (śūla), pravāhikā (straining at stool, tenesmus), distension (ādhmāna), cutting pain (parikarti), loss of appetite (aruci) and fevers (jvara). Thirst (tṛṣ), bewilderment (moha), burning (dāha), fainting (mūrcchā) and so on one should know as the complications (upadrava) of these.
notes:
line 05.06.126: GROUPING: 126 and 127 appear to form one statement; the verb vidyāt and the governing phrase 'upadravān' are in 127, so this unit is a bare list (no verb supplied). The final member is accusative plural (jvarān), the rest are compound members. Printed 'parikartyaruci' = parikarti + aruci (sandhi i+a = ya). 'parikarti' read as cutting pain (cf. parikartikā); standard.
line 05.06.127: GROUPING: appears to complete 126 (the list there and this list are the objects of vidyāt). 'tṛṇmoha' = tṛṣ + moha (ṣ-final becomes ṇ before m). 'eṣām' is not specified further in the unit (it refers to the varieties of 124-125).

hindi: वहाँ आम यानी अपक्व, अपचे पदार्थ में, अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, पान, कटु, अम्ल और लवण से युक्त, पाचन प्रशस्त है; आम में तो बस्ति का निषेध किया जाता है।
english: There, in āma (undigested matter), the drink — on a conjectural reading of the unclear word 'tara' — joined with pungent, sour and salty (ones), A digestive (pācana) is recommended; in āma, basti (enema) is indeed forbidden.

text_flags.why: possible: 'tarapāna' with avagraha is not a known word; 'antarapāna' is one guess (metre is unaffected); same form in 135

notes:
line 05.06.128: GROUPING: 128 and 129 appear to form one statement; the predicate 'pācanam śasyate' is in 129. The printed 'tarapānam' (after an avagraha) is unclear: no reading is built on it. Possible 'antara-pāna' (a drink taken between things) or 'itara-pāna', but neither is certain and neither is applied; the same word recurs in 135. Sandhi is regular otherwise.
OPEN (05.06.128) [minor] split / atara / pānam: Glossary: an unrestorable printed word is kept unsplit. The draft splits "atara" (the avagraha restored as a) from pānam, which builds a partial reading on the damaged word; same in 135. Owner may prefer a single unsplit word "'tarapānam" with gloss "unclear" (the patch tool cannot merge words). Suggested: (owner decision; no machine patch)
line 05.06.129: GROUPING: appears to continue 128. The grammar of 'pācanam' (neuter singular) with the drink of 128 is a natural reading but the link is not certain.

words.gloss: wind-destroying; binding (grāhin); belonging to the group

hindi: मल में वातनाशक और ग्राही यानी बाँधने वाले वर्ग की बस्ति प्रशस्त है। वायु में मधुर और अम्ल, स्पष्ट लवण वाली स्नेहबस्ति।
english: A basti (enema) of the group of wind-destroying and binding (grāhin) (ones) is recommended in stool. An oil enema (sneha-basti), sweet and sour, with the salt evident, in wind (samīraṇa).
notes:
line 05.06.130: 'grāhin' = binding, checking the bowels; kept as grāhi. 'vargīya' = belonging to the group (varga); the members of the group are not listed. 'in stool' is literal (śakṛti); what condition is meant is not stated.
line 05.06.131: Elliptical: no verb; 'is recommended' of 130 is carried over, none supplied. 'samīraṇa' (wind) is read as vāta; kept as 'wind'.

words.gram: caus. pass. pres. part., m. loc. sg. √sṛ

hindi: रक्त में, रक्त से, पित्त और रक्त में कसैला, मधुर और तिक्त। कफ के सरकाए जाते समय बस्ति कसैली, कटु और तिक्त।
english: In blood, with blood, in Pitta-and-blood (pittāsra): astringent, sweet and bitter. When Kapha is being made to move (sāryamāṇa), the basti is astringent, pungent and bitter.
notes:
line 05.06.132: Elliptical: the noun 'basti' is not in the line (carried from the series, none supplied). 'rakte raktena' is odd (locative then instrumental of the same word); the sense of the pair is not clear and no reading is built on it. 'pitta-asra' read as pitta-and-blood. Tastes: kaṣāya = astringent; the -ka ending is the usual adjectival suffix.
OPEN (05.06.132) [minor] notes / pittāsre / rakte raktena: pittāsra (and asṛkpitta, 143) is also the usual Sanskrit name of the disease raktapitta (bleeding disorder). The draft reads it as "pitta and blood" (consistent with the list of combinations, and kept), but add the alternative to the notes. "rakte raktena" (locative then instrumental of the same word) may be a corruption; unresolved. Suggested: (owner decision; no machine patch)
line 05.06.133: 'sāryamāṇe' read as the passive-causative present participle of √sṛ (being made to move or flow); this is the plain reading but not secure. No verb in the Sanskrit; 'is' supplied only as the copula of a locative absolute statement. Kaṣāya is the taste here (astringent), not a decoction.

hindi: मल से, अथवा वायु से, अथवा आम से; मल में, अथवा वायुओं से। संसृष्ट में, अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, पान कटु, अम्ल और लवण से युक्त हो।
english: With stool, or with wind, or with āma; in stool, or else with winds. In the mixed (case), there should be the drink — on a conjectural reading of the unclear word 'tara' — joined with pungent, sour and salty (ones).

text_flags.why: possible (very likely): the nukta-k stands for kṛ; same print habit in 143 'śaqacchoṇitayoḥ'
possible: final visarga dropped (the instrumental plural anilaiḥ is expected; metre needs 16 syllables as printed)
possible: same doubtful 'tarapāna' as in 128

notes:
line 05.06.134: GROUPING: 134 and 135 appear to form one statement (the predicate is in 135: saṃsṛṣṭe ... syāt). The line is a list of combinations (saṃsarga) and is odd: stool appears twice (śakṛt, varcas) and the cases vary (instrumental, locative); no reading is built on the sense. Print: 'śaqatā' (q is a nukta sign) for śakṛtā; final visarga of 'anilai' lost.
line 05.06.135: GROUPING: appears to complete 134. The word printed 'tarapānam' is unclear, as in 128 (see there); no reading is built on it. 'saṃsṛṣṭe' (mixed, combined) has no noun in the unit.

words.gloss: of the two that are mixed

hindi: पित्त से, आम में, रक्त से, उसी प्रकार; अथवा फिर उन दोनों का आम से। दो संसृष्टों में कटु, मधुर और तिक्त सहित पान हो।
english: With Pitta, in āma, with blood, likewise; or again, of those two, with āma. Of the two that are mixed, there should be a drink with pungent, sweet and bitter (tastes).
notes:
line 05.06.136: GROUPING: 136 and 137 appear to form one statement (predicate 'bhavet pānam' in 137). A list of combinations; the sense of 'tayoḥ āmena' (of/in the two, with āma) is not fully clear, so the literal order is kept; 'tayoḥ' could be genitive or locative dual.
line 05.06.137: GROUPING: appears to complete 136. 'saṃsṛṣṭayoḥ' (genitive or locative dual) has no noun in the unit; 'sa-kaṭuka' is read as 'with pungent' (kaṭuka = kaṭu).

hindi: उसी प्रकार कफ से संसृष्ट आम में कसैला, कटु और तिक्त। आम से तो कफ के युक्त होने पर कसैला, लव शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, औषध।
english: Likewise, in āma mixed with Kapha, (one) astringent, pungent and bitter. But when Kapha is joined with āma: a medicine (auṣadha), astringent and — on a conjectural reading of the doubtful word 'lava' — [salty].

text_flags.why: possible: the line is 15 syllables as printed and 16 with lavaṇa (ṇa dropped); not certain

notes:
line 05.06.138: Elliptical: 'pānam' (drink) of 137 is carried over (neuter ending), none supplied. Printed token "''me" = āme (double avagraha stands for ā). Kaṣāya here is the taste (astringent).
line 05.06.139: The compound 'kaṣāyalavauṣadham' is doubtful at 'lava': it may be a truncated lavaṇa (salt), which would give a 16-syllable line, but this is not certain and no reading is built on it. The English breaks off because the sense of the damaged word is not secure. kaṣāya = astringent taste or decoction: not fixed here.

lines_deva: वातेन विशि पित्ते वा विट्पित्तास्रे तथाऽनिले
lines_iast: vātena viśi pitte vā viṭpittāsre tathā'nile
hindi: वात से, मल में अथवा पित्त में; मल, पित्त और रक्त में, उसी प्रकार वायु में, संसृष्ट में कसैली, खट्टी और मधुर बस्ति उत्तम होगी।
english: With Vāta, in stool or in Pitta; in stool, Pitta and blood, likewise in wind, In the mixed (case), a basti astringent, sour and sweet would be best.

text_flags.why: possible: ś for ṣ; viṣ (viṭ) = excrement, locative viṣi; same form in 145

notes:
line 05.06.140: GROUPING: 140 and 141 appear to form one statement (predicate 'syāt ... bastiḥ uttamaḥ' in 141). Print 'viśi' read as viṣi (locative of viṣ/viṭ, excrement); the same print form recurs in 145. Pure list of combinations.
line 05.06.141: GROUPING: appears to complete 140. 'syāt' with 'uttamaḥ' is read as 'would be best'.

hindi: वात से और रक्त में बस्ति मधुर, अम्ल और तिक्त करनी चाहिए। मल और रक्त के, पित्त और मल के, रक्त और पित्त के,
english: With Vāta and in blood, the basti should be done sweet, sour and bitter. Of stool and blood, of Pitta and stool, of blood and Pitta,

text_flags.why: possible (very likely): the nukta-k stands for kṛ, as in 134

notes:
line 05.06.142: Literal: 'kāryaḥ' (should be done, made). 'with wind' and 'in blood' are the conditions as printed.
line 05.06.143: GROUPING: 143 and 144 appear to form one statement (predicate in 144: basti ... in mutual combination). Genitive or locative dual throughout, so 'of' is chosen; 'in' is also possible. Print 'śaqacchoṇitayoḥ' read as śakṛc-śoṇitayoḥ (sandhi śakṛt + ś = śakṛc-ch).

lines_deva: कफेन विशि पित्ते वा कफे विट्पित्तशोणितैः
lines_iast: kaphena viśi pitte vā kaphe viṭpittaśoṇitaiḥ
hindi: परस्पर संयोग में बस्ति कसैली, मधुर और तिक्त है। कफ से, मल में अथवा पित्त में; कफ में मल, पित्त और रक्त के साथ,
english: In mutual combination, the basti is astringent, sweet and bitter. With Kapha, in stool or in Pitta; in Kapha, with stool, Pitta and blood,

notes:
line 05.06.144: GROUPING: appears to complete 143. No verb in the Sanskrit; 'is' is the copula of the statement. 'anyonya' = one another (mutual).
line 05.06.145: GROUPING: 145 and 146 appear to form one statement (predicate in 146). 'viśi' is read as viṣi (see 140); flagged again for this occurrence.

hindi: संसृष्ट में कटु, तिक्त और कसैली बस्ति उत्तम होगी। वायु से संसृष्ट कफ में कटु, तिक्त और अम्ल बस्ति हो।
english: In the mixed (case), a basti pungent, bitter and astringent would be best. In Kapha mixed with wind, there should be a basti pungent, bitter and sour.

notes:
line 05.06.146: GROUPING: appears to complete 145. Print 'kadutikta...' read as kaṭutikta (the Devanagari has da for ṭa).
line 05.06.147: 'saṃsṛṣṭe' agrees with 'kaphe', with 'vāyunā' as the thing it is mixed with.

hindi: रक्त में, जो कफ से मिला हो, मधुर, उषण यानी तीखा और तिक्त। कफ से संसृष्ट वायु में कटु, अम्ल और लवण हो।
english: But in blood mingled with Kapha: sweet, uṣaṇa (pungent) and bitter. In wind mixed with Kapha, it should be pungent, sour and salty.
notes:
line 05.06.148: Elliptical: 'basti' of the series is carried over, none supplied. 'uṣaṇa' is read as the pungent taste (also pepper); if it is a misprint for uṣṇa the sense would be 'hot'. Not applied.
line 05.06.149: The subject (basti) is not stated; 'it' is used. Compare 147, where Kapha is mixed with wind.

words.gloss: three; four; five; six; by combining
words.gram: tat-puruṣa (dvandva of numbers + yoga), m. inst. sg.

hindi: तीन, चार, पाँच और छह के योग से इसी प्रकार विकल्प करे। और यह युक्ति, जो अतिसार यानी दस्त के लिए कही गई है, सब रोगों में भी मानी गई है।
english: By combining three, four, five and six, one should vary (it) in just this way. And this method (yukti), stated for atisāra (diarrhoea), is held also in all diseases.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āvem' is not a word; yogena + evam + eva gives 16 syllables and a sense

notes:
line 05.06.150: Printed 'yogenāvemeva' is read as yogena + evam + eva (naivameva garbled in the scan). The object of vikalpayet and the things combined are not stated.
line 05.06.151: Atisāra = diarrhoea (standard). 'atisāroktā' = atisāra-uktā, 'stated for/in atisāra'. 'smṛtā' = remembered, held (traditionally taught).

lines_deva: निरामार्णां तु पंचानां बस्तिः षड्रसिको हितः
lines_iast: nirāmārṇāṃ tu paṃcānāṃ bastiḥ ṣaḍrasiko hitaḥ
hindi: एक साथ, अस्पष्ट शब्द के अनुमानित पाठ पर, छह के संयोग में पाचन हो। आम से रहित पाँचों के लिए छह रसों वाली बस्ति हितकर है।
english: At once, on a conjectural reading of the unclear word 'sadrusam', in the combination of six, there should be a pācana (digestive). But of the five (ones) free of āma, a basti having six tastes is beneficial.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sadrusam' is not a word; ṣaḍ-rasam fits 153, metre is 16 either way
probable: stray r; nirāmāṇām (of those free of āma) is regular and keeps 16 syllables

notes:
line 05.06.152: 'sadrusam' is not a known word and is left unsplit and unread. It may be ṣaḍ-rasam (six tastes), as in 153 ṣaḍrasika, but that is only a guess and is not applied. Sense of the unit therefore uncertain.
line 05.06.153: Printed 'nirāmārṇām' has a stray r; nirāmāṇām is the regular genitive plural (ṇ after r is not blocked by m). The five are not named. 'ṣaḍrasika' = having six rasas (tastes).

lines_deva: शंखं सर्जरसं लाक्षां कत्तृणं च पलांशिकं
lines_iast: śaṃkhaṃ sarjarasaṃ lākṣāṃ kattṛṇaṃ ca palāṃśikaṃ

words.gloss: udumbara (cluster fig, Ficus racemosa; standard); unripe fruits
jambū (jamun, Syzygium cumini; probable, reading uncertain); mango (Mangifera indica; standard); udumbara; barks
sarja (sal tree, Shorea robusta); resin (sarjarasa; standard)

hindi: उदुम्बर यानी गूलर के शलाटु यानी कच्चे फल, जम्बू यानी सम्भवतः जामुन, आम्र यानी आम और उदुम्बर यानी गूलर की छालें। शंख, सर्जरस यानी साल का राल, लाख और कत्तृण यानी एक घास, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, और पल यानी तौल की इकाई के अंश वाला।
english: Unripe fruits (śalāṭu) of udumbara (cluster fig), the barks of jambū (probably jamun), āmra (mango) and udumbara. Conch shell (śaṅkha), sarjarasa (resin of the sal tree), lac (lākṣā) and kattṛṇa (a grass, unidentified), and with a pala as the portion.

text_flags.why: possible: jambu + āmra gives jaṃbvām; the printed 'byā' may be a misprint; metre is unchanged

notes:
line 05.06.154: GROUPING: 154 and 155 appear to be one list; 156 gives the preparation (piṣṭvā ... pacet). Printed 'jaṃbyāmra' (jambī/jambya + āmra) is read as jambū or jambu + āmra; possibly a misprint for jaṃbvāmra. 'śalāṭu' = unripe fruit (standard). The bark list is read as the barks of the three trees. Hindi names: गूलर, जामुन, आम.
line 05.06.155: GROUPING: appears to continue 154. 'palāṃśikam' is singular; whether it applies to all items (each one pala) is not stated, so the literal 'with a pala as the portion' is kept. Pala is a unit of weight. kattṛṇa unidentified here (earlier chunk: a grass, identity uncertain).
OPEN (05.06.155) [minor] notes / kattṛṇa: Some lexicons give kattṛṇa as a fragrant grass of the lemon-grass/rauhiṣa kind (Cymbopogon); I am not sure, so leave "unidentified" but the owner may record "possibly a fragrant Cymbopogon grass (disputed)". English "a grass, unidentified" and gloss "a fragrant grass" differ slightly. Suggested: (owner decision; no machine patch)

lines_deva: पिष्ट्वा तैः सर्पिषः प्रस्थं क्षीरद्विगुणितं पचेत्
lines_iast: piṣṭvā taiḥ sarpiṣaḥ prasthaṃ kṣīradviguṇitaṃ pacet
hindi: पीसकर उनके साथ एक प्रस्थ घी को, दूध से दुगुना किया हुआ, पकाए। सब अतिसारों में यह बल के अनुसार पीना चाहिए।
english: Having ground (them), one should cook with these a prastha (a measure) of ghee, doubled with milk. In all atisāras (diarrhoeas), this is to be drunk according to strength.
notes:
line 05.06.156: Appears to complete 154-155. 'kṣīradviguṇitam' = made twofold by milk (the amount of milk is thus twice the ghee on one reading); the text does not state the ratio, so the literal wording is kept. The grammar of the 'doubled' word (agreeing with prastha) is the plain reading.
line 05.06.157: 'this' refers to the ghee of 154-156. 'yathābalam' = according to the strength (of the patient is the natural sense, but the text does not say whose).

words.gloss: samaṅgā (disputed; Mimosa pudica is often given)
aśvattha (sacred fig, Ficus religiosa; standard); tips, shoots

hindi: कच्छुरा, धातकी यानी धाय, बिल्व यानी बेल, समंगा यानी सम्भवतः लाजवन्ती और रक्तमूली से, और मसूर तथा अश्वत्थ यानी पीपल के शृंग यानी अग्रभागों से, जल में उबालने पर, यवागू यानी लपसी हो।
english: With kacchurā, dhātakī (woodfordia), bilva (bael), samaṅgā (probably touch-me-not; disputed) and raktamūlin, And with masūra (lentil) and aśvattha (sacred fig) tips, boiled in water, there should be a yavāgū (gruel).
notes:
line 05.06.158: GROUPING: 158 and 159 appear to form one statement (yavāgū, 159). Identifications: kacchurā disputed (no botanical name given); dhātakī standard; bilva standard; samaṅgā disputed (Mimosa pudica often given); raktamūlin unidentified (read as 'red-rooted'). The last member is an instrumental plural, the others are compound members.
OPEN (05.06.158) [minor] notes / kacchurā / raktamūlin: kacchurā: lexicons variously give an Alhagi/durālabhā-type plant or Mucuna (kapikacchu); disputed, correctly not applied. raktamūlin: "red-rooted" is a literal guess only; unidentified, as the draft says. Suggested: (owner decision; no machine patch)
line 05.06.159: Appears to complete 158. 'masūraśvatthaśṛṅgaiḥ' is read as masūra + aśvattha-śṛṅga (shoots of the aśvattha); a reading of three separate items (masūra, aśvattha, śṛṅga) is also possible. Which of the things listed in 158-159 are boiled is not stated precisely.

words.gloss: young; udumbara (cluster fig); kaṭvaṅga (disputed; Oroxylum indicum often given); samaṅgā (see 158); plakṣa (probably Ficus virens, pilkhan; probable); sprouts
masūra (lentil); dhātakī (woodfordia); flowers; balā (country mallow, Sida cordifolia; standard)

hindi: कोमल गूलर, कट्वंग यानी सम्भवतः सोनापाठा, समंगा और प्लक्ष यानी सम्भवतः पाकड़ की कोंपलों से, और मसूर, धातकी यानी धाय के फूल और बला यानी खरैटी से भी उसी प्रकार हो।
english: With the sprouts (pallava) of young udumbara, kaṭvaṅga (probably Oroxylum indicum; disputed), samaṅgā and plakṣa (probably a fig, pilkhan), And with masūra, dhātakī flowers and balā (country mallow), it should be likewise.
notes:
line 05.06.160: GROUPING: 160 and 161 appear to form one statement (predicate 'tathā bhavet' in 161, i.e. likewise a yavāgū). Whether 'bāla' (young) governs only udumbara or all members is not clear; the plain reading is the first. Identifications: kaṭvaṅga disputed (Oroxylum indicum often given; some give Ailanthus); plakṣa probable (Ficus virens).
line 05.06.161: Appears to complete 160; 'it' is the yavāgū of 159 (not named in this unit). The compound 'masūradhātakīpuṣpabalābhiḥ' is read as masūra + dhātakī-puṣpa + balā; 'dhātakī flowers' is the plain reading, with 'masūra' a separate member.

hindi: बस्ति के विभ्रम यानी भूल से अनेक प्रकार की व्यापदें यानी दुर्घटनाएँ उत्पन्न होती हैं। मार्ग के अनुसार, अवस्था के अनुसार, उनका साधन यानी उपचार करे।
english: Mishaps (vyāpad) of various kinds arise from an error (vibhrama) in the basti. According to the path, according to the condition, one should carry out the treatment (sādhana) of those.
notes:
line 05.06.162: 'vibhrama' = error, deviation, confusion; kept as 'error'. 'nānāprakārā jāyante' is regular sandhi (āḥ before j). Here the chapter turns back to the mishaps of basti named in its title.
line 05.06.163: 'yathāpatham' is obscure: 'path' could mean the course or route of the mishap; a misreading for 'yathāpathyam' (as is suitable) is conceivable but not applied. 'sādhana' = accomplishing, treating; kept with a gloss.
OPEN (05.06.163) [minor] text_flags / yathāpatham: No flag is raised for the obscure yathāpatham. A possible-level flag to yathāpathyam ("as is wholesome") would be reasonable but is a guess; owner to decide. Translation "according to the path" is literal and left as is. Suggested: (owner decision; no machine patch)

hindi: इस प्रकार बस्तिव्यापत्सिद्धि नामक छठा अध्याय।
english: Thus the sixth chapter, named Bastivyāpatsiddhi.
notes: Chapter colophon (Kalpasthāna chapter 6). The closing 'iti' is the usual end-mark. Title as in line 05.06.1: basti-vyāpat-siddhi, 'accomplishment (success) concerning the mishaps of basti'.
